elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The Servicer indemnifies the Issuer and other customer-side Indemnified Persons, including under the new IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor defends Customer against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause reimburses defense costs and permits the Servicer to assume a defense, but does not impose an affirmative duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer's affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The defined Indemnified Persons include specified trustees, officers, directors, employees and agents, but not Customer affiliates generally.

elements.element: Vendor defends Customer's affiliates against the covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are not included and there is no affirmative defense duty.

elements.element: Vendor covers third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) covers systems, software and materials used by the Servicer in performing its obligations, but does not clearly cover the services themselves or all deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No indemnity trigger addresses the Servicer's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor covers third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach or security-incident indemnity trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(i) indemnifies for claims, actions, suits, losses and liabilities resulting from the Servicer's gross negligence or willful misconduct in performing its obligations.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires prompt notice of covered proceedings, subject to an appropriate prejudice limitation.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b) requires prompt notice and provides that failure does not impair indemnification except to the extent of prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure gives Vendor control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: The Servicer may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a proceeding at its expense.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires Customer to provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation is imposed on an Indemnified Person.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity is limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no Customer indemnity, so the condition for restricting such an indemnity is demonstrably absent and no broader Customer indemnity exposure is created.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer-side indemnitees against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning Vendor systems, software or other materials used in providing the contracted services.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) indemnifies the Indemnified Persons for third-party claims that systems, software or other materials used by the Servicer infringe or misappropriate any intellectual-property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) excludes claims to the extent resulting from modifications made or supplied by an Indemnified Person.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) excludes claims to the extent resulting from combinations made or supplied by an Indemnified Person.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) excludes claims to the extent resulting from specifications made or supplied by an Indemnified Person.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to procure the right to continue use of the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) requires the Servicer to procure the right to continue the affected use.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to modify the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) expressly permits modification of the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must have the option to replace the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(e) expressly permits replacement of the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procurement, modification and replacement are unavailable on commercially reasonable terms.
elements.evidence: If none of the preceding remedies is available on commercially reasonable terms, Section 6.3(e) requires a refund of the Servicing Fees paid for the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor's liability for the IP indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Liability under Section 6.3(e) is capped at three times the aggregate Servicing Fees paid during the twelve months preceding the claim.

result.reason: The redline reaches the complete fallback position by adding a third-party IP indemnity, the three specified exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3× trailing-twelve-month fee cap, without changing unrelated provisions. It does not reach the preferred position because it lacks an affirmative defense duty, affiliate coverage, breach-of-law and Vendor-caused data-breach triggers, cooperation language, and full services/deliverables IP coverage. Drafting quality is reduced by the ambiguous phrase “In that event,” which could refer to an excluded claim, and by tying the refund to fees paid for an “affected item” even though Vendor-used systems may not be separately fee-bearing.
